pointers.sentence: A project's template at one of those paths is found first, and by extending the admin's under the less specific name it changes one block and keeps the rest, as the documentation advises ([Inheritance and inclusion: `{% extends %}`, `{% block %}` and `{% include %}`](../templates/inheritance.md)) (`docs/ref/contrib/admin/index.txt`).
An attribute, `None` by default, replaces the list whole (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.render_change_form`).

*Without its attribute, a model admin's page tries the model's template and the application's before the admin's, the application index the application's; the index and the login try one name (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.app_index`).*

The logout and password pages take the auth views' own names ([The login and password views: `LoginView`, `LogoutView` and `PasswordChangeView`](../auth/login-views.md)), and the admin ships templates of those names in `django/contrib/admin/templates/registration/`, which a project's own replace (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.logout`).

The logout and password pages take the auth views' own names ([The login and password views: `LoginView`, `LogoutView` and `PasswordChangeView`](../auth/login-views.md)), and the admin ships templates of those names in `django/contrib/admin/templates/registration/`, which a project's own replace (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.logout`).

It keeps the choice in the render context under the node, where `InclusionNode.render` looks first; its comment says that setting the node's own file name would not be thread-safe, and with the default loaders the node belongs to a compiled template that the cached loader keeps for every request (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/base.py:InclusionAdminNode.render`, `django/template/engine.py:Engine.__init__`).

*The admin's inclusion tags: the change form's (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_modify.py`), then the change list's (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_list.py`).*
*The admin's inclusion tags: the change form's (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_modify.py`), then the change list's (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_list.py`).*

Other fragments have one name: a filter's `ListFilter.template` (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_list.py:admin_list_filter`), an inline's `InlineModelAdmin.template` ([Inlines: `InlineModelAdmin` and its formsets](inlines.md)), `"admin/includes/fieldset.html"`.

A widget's template goes through the form renderer, whose default engine skips a project's `"DIRS"` (`django/forms/renderers.py:EngineMixin.engine`): harbour's `"admin/widgets/related_widget_wrapper.html"` there was used, in a run, only once `FORM_RENDERER` named `TemplatesSetting` and `"django.forms"` was installed, without which Django's own form templates were not found ([Rendering a form: renderers and templates](../forms/rendering.md)).
`submit_row` decides the change form's buttons from what `render_change_form` puts in the context (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_modify.py:submit_row`).

`"admin/base_site.html"` extends it and fills `{% block title %}` and `{% block branding %}` from `AdminSite.site_title` and `AdminSite.site_header`, which `AdminSite.each_context` gives every page ([The site's own pages: the index, the login and `AdminSite.each_context`](site-views.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/templates/admin/base_site.html`).

It marks the current application and model by the request's path, which needs the request's context processor; the checks warn, as `"admin.W411"`, when that is missing ([The admin's checks: `check_dependencies` and `ModelAdminChecks`](checks.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/templates/admin/app_list.html`).
The theme button keeps its choice in the browser's local storage (`django/contrib/admin/static/admin/js/theme.js`).
`admin_urlname` makes such a name from a `_meta` and a suffix, and `admin_urlquote` quotes a key for a path (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_urls.py`).

`ModelAdmin.media` is a property listing, as a `Media`, the scripts of a model admin's change form, change list and delete pages ([Form assets: `Media`](../forms/media.md)), jQuery and XRegExp minified unless `settings.DEBUG` is true (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.media`).

`"admin/js/jquery.init.js"` moves the jQuery just loaded into `"django.jQuery"`; its comment says this leaves any jQuery of the page's own as it was (`django/contrib/admin/static/admin/js/jquery.init.js`).

`InlineModelAdmin.media` lists jQuery, `"admin/js/jquery.init.js"` and `"admin/js/inlines.js"`, and the two-box select's scripts with `filter_horizontal` or `filter_vertical` (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:InlineModelAdmin.media`).

A view adds the media of what its page holds: the change form, the `AdminForm`'s, its form's and so its widgets', each inline formset's and the action form's; the change list, the `list_editable` formset's and the action form's (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._changeform_view`, `django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.changelist_view`).

A view adds the media of what its page holds: the change form, the `AdminForm`'s, its form's and so its widgets', each inline formset's and the action form's; the change list, the `list_editable` formset's and the action form's (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._changeform_view`, `django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.changelist_view`).

The change form also loads the site's JavaScript catalogue, `AdminSite.i18n_javascript` ([The language views: `set_language` and `JavaScriptCatalog`](../i18n/views.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/templates/admin/change_form.html`).
`BaseModelAdmin` is made by `MediaDefiningClass`, so a model admin's inner `Media` adds to the property, unless its extend attribute says otherwise (`django/forms/widgets.py:media_property`).

Adding merges: in a run, a subclass of ShipAdmin made by hand with `js = ["fleet/tonnage.js"]` got its script before `"admin/js/jquery.init.js"`, and after it once its list began with that file, as the documentation asks of forms and widgets that use `"django.jQuery"` (`docs/ref/contrib/admin/index.txt`).

The admin's scripts, stylesheets and images are static files under `django/contrib/admin/static/admin/`, which the staticfiles application finds, and serves in development ([Serving static files: `StaticFilesHandler` and the development server](../contrib/serving-static.md)).
